advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope account_vote to the current patchset (filter votes by the current _revision/patchset number) so a stale vote from a prior patchset cannot satisfy the LLM-Review/Verified gate.
evidence: infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh:230: votes = (d.get("labels") or {}).get(label, {}).get("all") or []
Ticket 8f1b-ecd8-ea9e-42db AC: 'Wait for both current-patchset labels: LLM-Review +1 from the review bot and Verified +1 from the CI bot.'

The probe commit is pushed once and never amended in this flow, so in practice one patchset exists; but the reader itself does not distinguish patchsets, so if a re-push ever occurs the gate can accept a stale vote.
advisory.finding: account_vote reads votes from the DETAILED_LABELS 'all' array without scoping to the current patchset, so a stale Verified/LLM-Review +1 cast on an earlier patchset can satisfy the gate. The ticket AC requires both votes to be present on the tested/current patchset.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Match the voting account by exact username/identity rather than a case-insensitive substring of the display name so an unrelated account cannot satisfy the gate.
evidence: infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh:234: if who.lower() in name.lower() and v.get("value") is not None:
old code (removed in diff): 'if bot in name and v.get("value") is not None:'
CI_BOT_NAME default is a display-name string 'rebar CI bot' (line 75), matched as a substring rather than an exact account identity.
advisory.finding: The account-name match was loosened from case-sensitive exact-substring (`if bot in name`) to case-insensitive substring (`who.lower() in name.lower()`), and Verified now matches against the human-readable display name 'rebar CI bot'. A different account whose username/name contains that substring (case-insensitively) could satisfy the gate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make disposable-ticket cleanup robust to the task's actual initial status (or verify the created task's state) so a mismatched from-state does not silently leak the ticket.
evidence: infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh:109: rebar transition "$DISPOSABLE_TICKET" open closed --class obsolete \
infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh:110: --reason "reviewbot-e2e disposable trailer ticket cleanup" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
Cleanup is best-effort (|| true), so a wrong from-state produces no diagnostic and leaks the throwaway ticket.
advisory.finding: Disposable-ticket cleanup transitions 'open closed', assuming the freshly created task is in the 'open' state; if `rebar create task` produces a task in a different initial status the transition silently fails under `|| true` and the disposable ticket is leaked (never closed).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace source-text grep assertions in test_reviewbot_e2e.py with behavioral tests that execute the script's units (e.g. run the embedded python3 vote/sr parsers against sample Gerrit JSON, or run the script under a stubbed PATH asserting exit codes/side effects).
evidence: tests/scripts/test_reviewbot_e2e.py:9-10 `def _script() -> str:` / `return SCRIPT.read_text()`

infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh:1 `#!/usr/bin/env bash` — the grepped file is executable SOURCE UNDER TEST, not an instruction/config artifact, so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply

assertions such as `assert "poll_both_votes" in text`, `assert "create_ticket()" in text`, and `assert 'git commit -q -s -m "test: reviewbot e2e probe ${stamp}${TRAILER}"' in text` verify implementation text, not runtime behavior

Regression-blindness: the script could poll Verified but never break/enforce the gate, or the trailer could fail to land in the actual commit, and every assertion would still pass because the strings are present
advisory.finding: Every assertion in test_reviewbot_e2e.py greps the literal source text of the unit-under-test (the executable reviewbot-e2e.sh) rather than exercising its behavior — a source-grepping antipattern that cannot detect a behavioral regression and breaks on any behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. renaming poll_both_votes/ticket_id, restructuring the TRAILER assignment).
scenarios: A maintainer renames poll_both_votes or ticket_id, or reformats the TRAILER construction with identical runtime behavior — the tests fail with no real defect
A logic bug is introduced (e.g. the Verified `-lt` guard is inverted or the harness on missing Verified vote is dropped in a way that keeps the string) — the tests still pass
advisory.suggested_fix: Extract the vote-parsing and submit-requirement python3 snippets (account_vote, sr_status) into invocable form and drive them with representative Gerrit JSON fixtures asserting NONE/max/SATISFIED outputs; and/or run reviewbot-e2e.sh with stubbed rebar/gh/git/ssh on PATH, asserting the three terminal exit codes (PASS/BLOCKED/HARNESS) for engineered inputs.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the poll-before-submit ordering behaviorally (execute the script with stubs and assert submit is not attempted until both votes are observed) rather than via str.index positions dominated by header comments.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_reviewbot_e2e.py:37 `submit_pos = text.index("submitting change")`
tests/scripts/test_reviewbot_e2e.py:42-43 `assert text.index("LLM-Review") < submit_pos` / `assert text.index("Verified") < submit_pos`

infra/gerrit/reviewbot-e2e.sh:317 `log "submitting change #${CHANGE_NUM},${PATCHSET}…"` is the only 'submitting change' site; both 'LLM-Review' and 'Verified' first appear far earlier in the header comment, so the inequality is trivially true regardless of execution order
advisory.finding: The ordering assertions `text.index("LLM-Review") < submit_pos` and `text.index("Verified") < submit_pos` use str.index (first occurrence), which for these strings resolves inside the header comment block, so they assert documentation ordering rather than that the votes are actually awaited before the submit step executes — they cannot detect a regression that moves the submit before the poll.
scenarios: A refactor that emits the submit before the poll loop but keeps the header comment intact — the assertions still pass
